title: It was the best. Not anymore. [updated]
text:
Update: 

This app has strayed far from its original purpose as a comic reader. It suffers from an identity crisis—while it’s called Panels, its panel view feature is unreliable. Not only is it disabled by default, but it’s also labeled as experimental, making it feel like an unstable beta feature.

Beyond that, the developer’s response to issues is unprofessional—instead of offering help or solutions, they argue with users.

Worst of all, the app fails at its core function: reading comics. Even if your files are stored in iCloud, it clogs up your device’s storage until your phone becomes nearly unusable. Consider this a fair warning.


Previous Update: Important: Google Drive no longer support!!! 

The application has been reorganizing its features to implement a strategy where users pay for specific functionalities, aiming to generate consistent revenue. However, if you seek a reader that also allows you to enjoy comics shared online, whether on forums or from public Google Drive links, the developer has chosen not to support this morally. Additionally, the support provided is lacking, with feedback being met with a defensive attitude. Moreover, users are unable to access their own library from the root folder, even if it's stored in their iCloud account. Essentially, enjoying comics through the app requires sacrificing storage space, and to exacerbate matters, personal server files must also be downloaded to function. Ultimately, these numerous restrictions render the app practically unusable. ——— Previous review: This is the best comic library app in App Store! I don’t understand why this developer is doing such an excellent app for a very small market as digital comic readers demographic. I mean, this is an app that Apple might design if they were after comic readers. So well executed and so user friendly that it need to be charged as a prime pro price level. Congratulations to the developer and hoping others apps will be as excellent as this one is.

I love Panels on my iPad, so I was ecstatic when I saw it had finally come to Mac. While the interface is great, and it has dark mode unlike Simple Comic or YAC, I’ve run into some issues. First, it crashes. I’ve had the app freeze and crash on me while adjusting settings at least 3 times in the past 2 days. 
Finally, my biggest gripe: reversing reading order is finicky. I read almost exclusively manga, so it’s important that I’m able to read right to left. For some reason, the buttons you click to go backward and forwards do not reverse when reversing reading order, although your arrow keys do. I’ve also run into issues with the scroll wheel. It may just be my mouse, but scrolling a single page requires at least two full spins of the scroll wheel which is not easy to do. Being able to adjust scroll sensitivity would help this. It would also be nice to be able to use the vertical scroll wheel on your mouse to scroll your comic horizontally if you choose. 

Please fix reverse reading order and the scroll wheel sensitivity and this could be 5 stars!

title: Great Reading, Clean Interface, Terrible Organizing..
text:
Panels is slick. It looks good and it’s clean and smooth, however, it’s abysmally bad when it comes to importing and organizing comics.

Older comic fans might remember ComicZeal, an app that unfortunely became abandonware, but I stuck with it until it became unusable on ios17. Why? Because it auto-organized comics for you. You could import a hundred comics into ComicZeal and it sorted things out for you. If a title already had a folder, it added new comics to the folder, and if it found several comics with the same title with no existing folder, you could tell it to auto-create new folders based on the titles of the comic books. It meant that importing, organizing, and finding your comic books was easy. Did it sometimes (rarely) mess up? Sure, but you could search for any comics that didn’t land properly and very quickly put them in the right place. It saved a TON of time.

In Panels, unless you’re importing pre-organized folders directly into the app folder with a desktop utility, then importing any quantity of comic books is a nightmare, and you’ll spend literal hours trying to organize things. I and others have asked the developers for auto-organizing features for years and they always have some excuse, making it sound as if ‘user agency’ amounts to wasting hours of user time to do something an app should be able to easily handle!

It’s insane that they refuse to add functionality that existed 10 years ago in an older app, and which makes panels ridiculously tedious to use unless your comics are pre-sorted or unless you only plan to import a dozen or two issues.

Tedious. Tedious. Tedious.

title: Decent But Flawed
text:
This is a serviceable comics reader, with two major issues. 1) Importing comics can be cumbersome. Unlike the old ComicsZeal, there is no support for importing more than one collection (ie. series) at a time; if you important a bunch of issues spread across multiple series, you need to manually organize them in the app after import. 2) The feature allowing you to share your reading progress across multiple devices doesn’t work well—shame, since that would be very useful.

UPDATE: After using this app a lot since I wrote the above, I’m seeing additional issues. 1) Frequent freezes, requiring a Force Quit (happens at least once or twice per reading session). 2) The app is sometimes confused by the file names inside older cbr files, and therefore doesn’t display pages in the correct order. 3) Thumbnails for issue covers are often wrong; you’ll see the same thumbnail for multiple issues in a collection

title: Polished for a Jagged Rock
text:
This is one of the better readers from a basic UI standpoint, but probably one of the worst from a technical one. 

You can add files through iTunes, but not whole folders. As for retrieving them from the app, you might as well forget it. You must create the folders in the app separately, either to import into or add to later. These folders also become part of the app and cannot be managed anywhere else. It’s an overly tedious design that hints at poor development or excessive attempts to force subscription without first building the trust that it will be any less tedious.

Subscriptions meant to cover the cost of services make sense. After all, some do charge the developers. Lumping in services that the developers don’t pay a dime to maintain should be a separate, one-time fee to cover the cost of publishing the app. I can’t see paying Panels monthly to cover the cost of using my local server, unless they plan to send out techs to maintain it. After my experience importing files, I wouldn’t want to pay for that experience again.

There is almost no animation to reading beyond the generic slide. For one of the most expensive apps to own, it is sad to fall short of the stock Books app included by Apple.

Overall, I like the basic look of the UI and hope that one day the functionality catches up. Until then, I will continue to sync with Chunky and import the files here to organize when I get to it. If not for the UI, I probably wouldn’t bother at all.

title: Buona ma...
text: L'app ha una bella interfaccia ma ha un bug fastidiosissimo: quasi sempre, importando i file cbr da cartelle locali, i file restano nella lista degli "incoming" e non vengono importati nella libreria, costringendomi a ricorrere ad iTunes. Per un'app che si dichiara la migliore mi sembra un bug piuttosto grave.
